scenes.title: Commutative property of addition
scenes.problem: Compare 18 + 27 and 27 + 18. Calculate and name the property that justifies the comparison.
actions: Write 18 + 27 and identify the complete groups and operation.
Swap the two addends; their sum stays the same. Represent 18 + 27 with its numbers, not an unrelated picture.
Apply commutative property of addition: 18 + 27 corresponds to 27 + 18.
Calculate both sides: 18 + 27 = 45 and 27 + 18 = 45. Verify against the original question.
scenes.memo: 18 + 27 = 27 + 18 = 45. This is commutative property of addition; the original expression gives 45.
scenes.misconception: Do not change the operation, drop a factor, or treat division by zero as zero.

scenes.title: Division by zero is undefined
scenes.problem: Is 29 ÷ 0 defined? Explain why a quotient cannot be formed.
actions: Write 29 ÷ 0 and identify the complete groups and operation.
No number of zero-sized groups can make the original dividend. Represent 29 ÷ 0 with its numbers, not an unrelated picture.
Apply division by zero is undefined: 29 ÷ 0 corresponds to no whole-number quotient.
No quotient exists. Verify against the original question.
scenes.memo: 29 ÷ 0 is undefined: division by zero is not a valid whole-number operation.
scenes.misconception: Do not change the operation, drop a factor, or treat division by zero as zero.
